records.deidentified_narrative: unit one pulled behind its residence at [roadway]. the driver and passenger of unit one exited the vehicle at the mouth of their garage. the driver of unit one failed to properly set brakes and put the vehicle in park. unit one began to roll from its position northbound towards a property line fence. the driver and passenger attempted to stop unit one's momentum from outside the vehicle. both were knocked to the ground, and suffered minor injures. unit one continued rolling northbound unoccupied. unit one then struck the property line fence that bordered [roadway]. unit one broke through the privacy fence damaging a 20 foot section of fence and support poles. unit one then fell off a 2. 5 foot retaining wall and continued northbound. the impact with the fence caused 6-bd-2 damage to unit one. after the retaining wall unit one traveled roughly 400 feet before impacting the parked/unoccupied unit two. unit two was parked at [roadway] facing west. the impact from unit one caused 9-lbq-1 damage to unit two and 6-bd-1 damage to itself. unit one also damaged trees, shrubs, and solar landscape lights at [roadway]. the property owners at 10006 and 10009 stony point were made aware of the damaged property. the occupants of unit one were evaluated by east texas medical and refused treatment or transport. unit one was returned under its own power to the owners at [roadway]. end of report

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at 1120 hours i, officer allison, [medical facility] ([roadway]) was informed by peter tucker (witness) that an individual was struck by a vehicle in the [medical facility] and the vehicle fled the scene. i walked to the north east parking lot area where peter [roadway] and observed a h/m (later identified as pirir gabino who is the listed victim) holding his left hand close to his body and it appeared he was injured from his bodily language. another h/m (jose chamale, listed witness) was standing with pirir at the time i walked up. both pirir and jose had backpack blowers and appeared to [medical facility] for lawn care. i attempted to speak with pirir but due to a language barrier jose translated for pirir. jose informed me pirir was blowing grass and leaves off the parking lot when a white pickup struck him causing him to roll to the ground and injure his hand. i asked jose if pirir was claiming injury and wanted to file a report. jose informed me pirir was claiming injury to his left hand and shoulder and did want to file a report. jose informed me he was blowing grass and leaves off the parking lot when he observed pirir already on the ground and a white extended cab truck near pirir. jose said the truck was driven a w/m but was unable give a [roadway]. jose said the truck left and the driver never attempted to check on pirir [medical facility] due to his injuries and jose translated he would go later to have it look at. i was later informed [medical facility] after i spoke with him. i spoke with a witness deanna williams who informed me she observed a white truck strike an h/m (pirir gabino) who was blowing grass and leaves off the parking lot. deanna said the truck stopped to keep from running over the h/m and then left the scene without ever checking on the h/m that was struck. deanna was able to record the lp to the suspect vehicle and gave the lp of tx lp bsv-6619. i spoke with pam williams who also witnessed the white truck strike pirir and flee the scene without getting out checking pirir's welfare. i spoke with peter tucker again who was the original reporting party and notified me of the hit and run. peter informed me he observed a white extended cab truck strike the h/m (pirir gabino) landscape worker and flee the scene. witnesses: 1: jose chamale, (903) 917-8808; deanna williams, (903)331-8448; pam williams, (903) 707-9761; peter tucker, (903) 576-8513.================================================================ on [date], i, officer grisham, added unit 1 driver and vehicle information to the report.

records.deidentified_narrative: [roadway] #1 is designated for left turns onto hercules west/bound and lanes #2, 3, and 4 are designed to travel north bound. the driver of unit 2 (jesus gonzalez) [roadway] #4 and advised that he observed something [roadway] in front of him but could not identify what it was. jesus gonzalez advised that he thought it was a bag of trash or a roll of carpet. the driver had a green light at the intersection of dyer and hercules and due to heavy traffic, he could not swerve to avoid the object in the roadway. the pedestrian was within the crosswalk, but was in the roadway when traffic on dyer (heading n/b) had a green signal. the driver struck the pedestrian on the south side of the intersection and the body was pulled under the vehicle and dragged the pedestrian across the intersection to the north side of the intersection. the vehicle was stuck and could no longer move forward due to the pedestrian preventing further [roadway] the vehicle in reverse in order to identify what he had collided with, at which time, jesus gonzalez identified a pedestrian and immediately pulled over to a safe area by 8300 dyer until authorities arrived. rescue #16 was dispatched at approximately 2108 hours and arrived on scene at approximately 2110 hours and found the pedestrian lifeless. sti units #10 (sgt. garcia #1375), 11(ofc. gomez #2710), and 12 (ofc. hatch #2837) arrived and conducted their investigation of the scene. officers towed the vehicle (nissan altima) to 11615 railroad and held it for sti for further investigation. the driver of the vehicle (jesus gonzalez) signed a consent to search form prior to the vehicle being towed and officers on scene observed an orange glass smoking pipe with marihuana residue inside. officers cited jesus gonzalez (citation [identifier]) for possession of drug paraphernalia. extreme towing arrived at 0235 hours and towed to vehicle to 11615 railroad.

records.deidentified_narrative: i-10 west at exit 25 is a 4-lane roadway for westbound vehicular traffic. pedestrian-1 was traveling westbound on i-10 in his vehicle, when he stopped in the #1 lane to render aide/assist another vehicle (tx/paper plates-509425f) which was in the #2 lane of travel and appeared to have been in a motor vehicle accident (eppd crash #18-153045). pedestrian-1 walked over to the mentioned vehicle. edward cienfuegos had also seen the mentioned vehicle and stopped on the right shoulder of i-10 west. once pedestrian-1 and [person] the vehicle was unmovable, they observed another vehicle (tx-[identifier]) on the left shoulder of i-10 west, just east of their location. as pedestrian-1 and [person] eastbound on i-10 west, unit-1 was traveling westbound on i-10 west towards pedestrian-1 and [person]. as [person] to head to the median that divides i-10 west and east, pedestrian-1 continued to walk eastbound. once unit-1 got closer to pedestrian-1, pedestrian-1 began heading to the median, but was struck by unit-1 before being able to jump over the median onto i-10 east. pedestrian-1s body was flung over onto the #1 lane of i-10 east, where it laid at rest. witness-1 (edward cienfuegos): stated he observed a vehicle (tx/paper plates-509425f) in the #2 lane. cienfuegos observed pedestrian-1 walking to the vehicle, at which time cienfuegos parked his vehicle and went to assist pedestrian-1. cienfuegos realized the vehicle was unmovable, they both observed another vehicle (tx-[identifier]) on the left shoulder of i-10 west, just east of their location. as they both were walking eastbound on i-10 west, unit-1 struck pedestrian-1. witness-2 (tavizon, armando) stated that he was traveling westbound on i-10 west in the #2 lane, when he observed unit-1 coming up behind him at a high rate of speed. he then observed unit-1 pass (go around) him and continued westbound, subsequently striking pedestrian-1.
